mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP signals a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of GDP growth compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of rising unemployment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in industrial production signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of declining industrial production compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts by more than 5% in a month signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which reduces related economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of declining housing starts compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong payroll growth compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.3% month-over-month, the combination signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tightening monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of high inflation and high interest rates compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth is positive and housing starts are increasing, the combination signals a strong demand side of the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: economic expansion with strong housing demand
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of positive GDP growth and increasing housing starts compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
